name: Shopwatch
description: Cycle-time measurement for the shop floor, arranged around the tool layout: the tooling for one operation and the machines that run it, with a number of its own. One layout can be run on several machines — identical machines share an arrangement rather than each keeping a copy — while every recorded cycle names the machine it was taken on, so their times stay apart. The screen opens on the floor: the cells, the operations that run in each, and the layout each is run as with its machines and its pockets. Search for a machine by name and it answers with that machine's tool layouts sorted by operation, timed as they run there. Nothing is pulled up until a tool is picked. Cutting time is measured at the machine rather than typed, the layout's cycle is charted across its tools, a part's route across the cells is drawn as a value stream map, and both print — one tool layout to a page. CSV in and out.
